title: Quant‑Aware Prompt Localization and Fidelity Contract
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This document describes the operational process, acceptance criteria, and monitoring contract for localizing prompt sets for production services when the target inference fleet uses quantized model variants. The goal is to enable reliable, measurable localization (language, region, formal/informal tone) while bounding the fidelity impact introduced by quantization and runtime optimizations (KV cache, batching).

Context and motivation
----------------------
As Redwood serves international customers and expands Dedicated/Private deployments, teams frequently adapt prompts to local idioms and regulatory constraints. Many deployments prefer quantized model variants to reduce cost and latency. Quantization can change surface-level tokenization and subtle generation characteristics, increasing the risk of meaning drift when prompts are localized. This guide codifies a cross-team contract between prompt owners, model-onboarding, and the eval-harness team to certify localized prompt families before rollout.

Goals
-----
- Create a reproducible, low-friction workflow for translating and adapting prompt families with automated checks against quantized inference artifacts.
- Define fidelity thresholds (the "Fidelity Contract") that must be met by any localized prompt-version pair for production promotion.
- Integrate checks into shadow/onboarding pipelines so regressions are detected pre-rollout.
- Provide a triage/playbook for when localized prompts fail fidelity checks.

Scope
-----
This guide covers text-only prompt localization for generation and reranking services (chat, completion, rerank). It does not cover multimodal prompt assets (images/audio) or customer-supplied proprietary translations (those follow private-deployments localization rules).

Key concepts and definitions
----------------------------
- Source prompt family: canonical prompt templates in English or origin language.
- Localized prompt: adapted prompt for a target locale.
- Quantized artifact: model binary/weights using per-channel INT8 or hybrid FP16/INT8 quantization that will be used in the target fleet.
- Fidelity Contract: pass/fail rules and numeric thresholds describing acceptable degradation in quality and behavior for a localized prompt under quantized inference.
- Response Stability Index (RSI): internal metric combining semantic similarity (S-BERT cosine), token-level divergence, and safety-rule violation counts. RSI ranges from 0.0 (diverged) to 1.0 (identical).

Fidelity Contract (must pass all clauses)
----------------------------------------
1) RSI >= 0.92 when comparing localized prompt outputs on quantized artifact vs. baseline outputs on reference (non-quantized) artifact, aggregated over the canonical probe slice.
2) Safety sentinel pass rate >= 99.5% across the localized probe set (no new safety categories introduced).
3) Latency uplift <= 12% p95 compared to the baseline quantized artifact on the same hardware profile (ensures localization does not induce pathological prompt tokens that harm batching/KV paths).
4) Coherence drop <= 1.5 percentage points on the task-specific coherence metric (e.g., factuality or instruction-following accuracy).

Measurements and test harness
----------------------------
All measurements are run via the eval-harness runner (service: eval-fleet) with the following configuration table: 

| Parameter | Required value / notes |
| --- | --- |
| runner mode | shadow (production mirror) + replay; synthetic seed size >= 200 per locale |
| model artifacts | reference (FP16) and target quantized build hashes (provide both) |
| seed randomness | fixed RNG seed across runs for determinism; record seed in metadata |
| telemetry tolerance | capture top-3 beam outputs, CSR token logs, KV-cache hit/miss |
| sampling | deterministic decoding (beam/greedy) for RSI calculation; sample-based stochastic checks for human-like variance tests |

Localization workflow (step-by-step)
------------------------------------
1. Owner (product/feature) creates a localized prompt branch in the prompt registry with locale metadata (language, region, tone).
2. Prompt author runs the local preflight script: `tools/prompt-localize/validate_localized_prompt --locale fr-FR --sample 250 --baseline-hash <ref-hash> --target-hash <quant-hash>` which executes the eval-harness smoke tests.
3. If smoke tests pass, open a Model Onboarding ticket and attach localization artifacts, probe slice IDs, and eval run IDs.
4. Model Onboarding schedules a gated shadow-run against the quantized artifact using the eval-fleet with the configuration above.
5. Automated acceptance checks evaluate the Fidelity Contract. If the contract passes, the patch is marked `localization-ready` and deployed to canary traffic (1%).
6. Canary run (minimum 72 hours or 100k tokens, whichever comes first). Continuous monitoring of RSI and safety sentinels.
7. If canary metrics remain within contract bounds, promote to rollout and record the localization certificate in the prompt manifest.

Automated checks and example CLI outputs
--------------------------------------
- RSI check (example output):
  `RSI: 0.943 (threshold 0.92) — PASS`
- Safety sentinel (example):
  `safety_failures: 0 new categories, pass_rate: 99.96% — PASS`
- Latency (p95) check:
  `p95_quant: 142ms (baseline_quant: 128ms) — uplift 10.9% — PASS`

Triage and remediation playbook (when checks fail)
--------------------------------------------------
1. Failures automatically create a triage card in the model-regression backlog with prefilled fields: prompt id, locale, quant-hash, RSI delta, example divergent outputs.
2. Owner and Model Onboarding perform a quick human review within 24 hours to decide classification: 
   - prompt-author-fixable (typo/phrase causing tokenization issues),
   - quant-artifact issue (unexpected quant noise),
   - intent-shift (localization introduced ambiguous phrasing), or
   - runtime-induced (KV/batching causing degradation).
3. Remediation steps by classification: 
   - prompt-author-fixable: update prompt and re-run preflight (fast path).
   - quant-artifact issue: escalate to runtime/quant team; schedule microprofiling run with kernel and token traces.
   - intent-shift: engage localization SMEs to rephrase and add anchor examples to the probe set.
   - runtime-induced: adjust batching/config, or pin to higher-capacity instance for that locale.
4. If remediation is blocked >72 hours, rollback localized variant and open a postmortem (owner: prompt author, reviewer: model-onboarding).

QA and human-in-the-loop checks
-------------------------------
- For high-risk slices (financial, healthcare, legal), require human review of at least 50 random localized outputs during canary.
- Annotator rubric: binary accept/reject and a short comment; the localization owner must remediate any >5% reject rate.

Telemetry and dashboards
------------------------
- Dashboards integrated into the Redwood Console: per-locale RSI timeseries, safety sentinel trends, and latency delta overlays.
- Alerting: RSI drop > 0.03 in 1 hour or safety pass rate < 99% triggers a P2 oncall page.

Ownership and operational contacts
----------------------------------
- Prompt registry owners: Content Platform (team alias: content-platform@redwood.ai)
- Model Onboarding: onboarding@redwood.ai
- Eval Harness / Runner: eval-infra@redwood.ai
- Quantization/runtime team: inference-kernels@redwood.ai

Rollout checklist (pre-promotion)
--------------------------------
1. All automated Fidelity Contract checks: PASS.
2. Required human reviews completed and recorded in the prompt manifest.
3. Canary monitoring configured with RSI, safety, and latency widgets.
4. Related run artifacts (hashes, seed, probe slices) uploaded to the eval registry.
5. Deployment playbook and rollback steps documented on the ticket.

Appendix A — Example probe slice manifest (plain text table)
-----------------------------------------------------------
| slice_id | description | sample_size | risk_class | primary_metrics |
| SLC-LOC-FR-001 | formal-customer-support-fr | 500 | medium | RSI, safety_sentinals, coherence |

Appendix B — Quick debugging commands
-------------------------------------
1) Run deterministic RSI locally against both artifacts: `python -m eval_harness.runner --probe SLC-LOC-FR-001 --baseline <fp16-hash> --target <int8-hash> --mode compare --seed 42`
2) Capture tokenization differences: `tools/token-diff --prompt-file localized.txt --baseline-encoding ref.enc --target-encoding quant.enc`
3) Generate human review bundle: `tools/annotation/export_bundle --slice SLC-LOC-FR-001 --n 100 --format csv`

Document maintenance and review cadence
-------------------------------------
This document is owned by the Applied ML Evals guild. Reviewers listed above should revisit thresholds and tooling references quarterly or when a major quant-kernel change lands. Any update must include an explicit migration plan for active localized prompts.

-------------------------
